# Pending changes (since patch 0017, 2026-11-22)

## 2026-11-22 - Every empire its own: people, ships, stations, hangars, towns

Asked: "go through all npcs, stations and spaceships and improve the graphics based on existing
references. improve graphics for buildings too, populate stations not with automatons but with npcs of the
empire that the station belongs to".

References used: external/images/<empire>_ships_1.png and <empire>_spacestations_1.png (each empire's sheet),
art/<empire>/ and art/guard, art/pirate, art/kilon, art/player (the 2D sprites), external/images/minoan_npc_*,
npc_pirate_*, kilon_alios_sheet, player_on_foot_*; data/sprites/tile_<empire>_* (each empire's building tiles).

Done:
- **The empires' look** (EmpireKit, was MinoanKit; shaders/world/empire.gdshader, was minoan.gdshader): an
  empire is a material - its colours (main, accent, second accent, iron, steel, gold, lamps), its **emblem**
  (the Minoan triskelion and bull, Athens' owl in a laurel, Sparta's lambda, Mycenae's rosette, Ionia's
  lyre, the Cyclades' spiral, the Sea Peoples' skull, a star for the independents) on roundels, banners
  and crates, its **frieze** (wave, meander, lambdas, rosettes, spirals, teeth), how worn its paint is,
  masonry (each block its own tone) or veined marble - all drawn in the shader. New zones: gold, a second
  accent. The Mesher gains slabs cut to an outline (wings, sails), smooth oval lofts. Emblems, friezes
  and banners on a station are floodlit (seen on its unlit side).
- **Stations** (CosmosStation): each empire's own design, from its sheet -
  Athens: a marble ring under navy roofs, gold cornices, the meander; four temples on it (colonnades,
  pediments, the owl); a tholos in the middle (a round colonnade under a cone, the owl on its crown), stoas;
  Sparta: an eight-sided fortress of iron under cream and crimson armour, a bastion at each corner (the
  lambda on its roof, a turret), gold spear tips, an eight-sided keep;
  Mycenae: a citadel of great uneven blocks, red bands, gold studs, rosettes; a corbelled tholos dome, gold
  rosette shields on its stone arms;
  Ionia: an armillary - a slim marble ring inlaid with lapis, a second ring, a lapis dome with three gold
  rings turned round it, arms ending in volutes;
  the Cyclades: two arms of white marble winding out from a dome to a slim ring, a marble figure on the dome;
  the Sea Peoples: a broken ring of dark iron, bone spikes, red plates, teeth, the skull, crooked masts;
  the independents: a plain tower, a ring, solar wings. The Minoans' as before.
  Shared: the ring holds still; four railed, floodlit platforms of pads out from it; shafts and shutters.
- **Stations as data**: a station's ~400-570 boxes and cylinders were nodes made and freed at load (15-33 ms
  a station); now plain data (Part), its decoration recorded as it's laid out (Dress) and played back by the
  worker that bakes it all into one mesh (7,000-18,000 triangles, 25-60 ms off the main thread). Laid out in
  one loading step (4-6 ms), its solids and the bake's start in the next (7-9 ms).
- **Ships** (EmpireHulls, new; CosmosHull): each empire's small ships (patrols, raiders) and big ones
  (traders), two variants each, one mesh a design, made on workers, shared, scaled to the ship -
  Athens: marble and navy, scythe wings forward or a delta with the meander; the traders carry a temple;
  Sparta: iron under cream and crimson, the lambda on an eight-sided shield, swept wings, gun barrels;
  Minoa: cream and red, twin prow horns, the double axe's blades for wings (traders: your ship's kind);
  Mycenae: stone blocks banded in gold, boar's tusks at the bow, a gold dome with the rosette;
  Ionia: marble and lapis, an Ionic column across the hull with volutes, curling wings;
  the Cyclades: one smooth piece of white marble, a curled prow, oars of ribs, the spiral;
  the Sea Peoples: dark iron and red, scythes, bone spikes, a tattered sail with the skull; independents:
  plain grey and orange. Engines glow in the empire's lamp colour. A ship is launched once its hull is made.
- **People** (Blender: external/blender/automaton; art/<id>_3d) -
  the Minoan android and the palace guard rebuilt on a body of their own (minoan.py): a big beaked
  triceratops head with long brow horns, a scalloped frill as wide as the shoulders (bands, petals, spirals,
  knobs), layered chest plates round a glowing core, round pauldrons with roundels, a meander belt and a
  short apron (the long kilt gone), heavy armoured legs, three-toed clawed feet;
  five new: **athenian** (a horned, owl-eyed theropod in marble and navy, the owl in a laurel), **spartan**
  (a bronze tyrant with a red helmet crest, crimson plates, lambdas), **mycenaean** (a gold death-mask
  pachycephalosaur, a studded red dome, rosettes), **ionian** (a lapis duck-bill with a long gold crest,
  volutes), **cycladic** (a pale idol with a long snout and one dark fin, thin spirals);
  the **pirate** (a real tricorn with skull flaps, a helmet with red slits, a long tattered coat with the
  skull and tentacles on its back, red lacquer pauldrons, hoses, a heavier rifle), **Kilon Alios** (a deep
  pointed hood over a masked face, an open coat to the ankles with lapels, straps and pockets, sleeved arms),
  your **automaton** (a domed helmet in one mask with slanted eyes, sculpted breastplate, boxy rimmed
  pauldrons, four fingers, a longer rifle with a scope).
  Triangles drawn: 15,700-20,400 an android, 22,400 the automaton, 30,600 the pirate, 28,600 Kilon.
- **Towns' people**: each empire's own model (CosmosNpc.people_id / dress; the recolouring only where an
  empire has no model of its own).
- **Hangars** (CosmosHangar): every empire's bay in its look - its emblem great on the back wall, on the
  banners and the crates, its frieze along the walls, pillars (round columns under capitals for Athens,
  Ionia, the Cyclades; gold-banded for Sparta and Mycenae), galleries, crate stacks, a gantry crane, the
  terminals' screens; pale marble halls or dark iron. **Its crew: nine of the empire's own people** (an
  independent station: from every empire), two of them armed and on guard by the terminals; each uses the
  standing and walking clips its model has. The hall lit all round (AMBIENT_HALL) so they're seen.
- **Towns** (CosmosTown.Builder by empire; building.gdshader): Athens - marble ashlar, Doric columns, the
  meander band, a peristyle temple under a tiled gable with pediments, a gable on the great hall, acroteria;
  Sparta - grey limestone on a crimson foot, bronze shields along the walls, lambdas, a gabled hall;
  Mycenae - cyclopean masonry (many-sided blocks in the shader), a gold band, the relieving triangle over
  doors, rosettes, a beehive tholos with its passage; Ionia - marble between lapis bands, slim lapis columns
  under gold volutes, egg and dart, gold armillaries on roofs, a temple; the Cyclades - white cubes, blue
  bands and blue domes, square pillars, marble figures before a domed chapel. Altars carry each empire's
  own sacred thing. The Minoans' as before.
- **Loading** (the bar: no frame over 33 ms): the scripts and scenes a first game needs and the people's
  models loaded on a thread at the title (CosmosWarm.PRELOAD); the HUD's own font and all its sizes drawn
  there (it had warmed another font: a 20 ms first draw); materials drawn at the title kept for the run (a
  standard material's shader is dropped with the last material using it - made again at the first station);
  the pad numbers' font 512 -> 128 (15 ms of glyphs); the hold's crates instances of two meshes (stacking
  the cargo made a mesh: 15 ms); the build's last steps (ship, camera, HUDs) a frame each, the game HUD
  shown a piece a frame; the galaxy's goods planned in a frame of their own; the arrival's autosave 0.4 s on.
  New game from the title: worst frame 250 -> 35-48 ms (still over the bar: two frames of first drawing,
  ~30 ms, not yet traced); a gate jump 65 -> 16-27 ms (within it).
- Docs: the guide's stations, ships, hangar and towns lines; CLAUDE.md. Shots retaken (the digger put away
  and the target cleared before the town's shots). Test: test_every_empire_builds_its_own.

Numbers: 7 station designs + the independents'; 8 ship liveries x 2 sizes x 2 variants (350-5,000 triangles);
12 character models; frame rate - every scenario within its baseline (by the station 833, a town 550, a
pirate camp 557, a hangar 786 FPS).

## 2026-11-22 - A jump without the flip; the jet pack, up to space; the empires' own town names

Asked: "fix the jump animation of the android, there is a flip roll that i dont like, add also a jet pack
animation for when i keep space pressed, jet pack can be upgraded to jump higher and higher until finally
have the ability to fly to space as an automaton without a ship"; then "complete all other tasks".

Done:
- **The jump**: on foot the "air" clip was the combat leap (a full somersault, its body raised a metre in the
  clip on top of the walker's own rise). Three new clips for your automaton (moves.py, baked and exported:
  art/player_3d, 33 clips): **jump** (a push off, the arms swinging up, the knees drawn up a little at the
  top - upright), **fall** (a loop: arms out for balance, legs stirring), **jet** (hovering: legs together
  and hanging back, toes pointed, arms down and out, a slow bob and sway). No "air" in them: the walker
  rises and falls itself, the feet hang from the pelvis.
- **The jet pack** (CosmosWalker): on its back on the chest's bone (EmpireKit's Minoan look: a frame, two
  tanks with red bands, nozzles, lamps, the roundel), a flame from each nozzle (the ship's engine shader).
  Jump, keep Space held: after 0.22 s it fires - a climb while its charge lasts, refilled on the ground in
  1.5 s; the body leans into its flight across. Levels (an automaton upgrade - Leg Servos: Jet pack, five
  levels, 900 credits up; shown as "level N"): [charge s, thrust m/s2, top climb m/s] 0: 0.7 / 17 / 6 (~6 m
  up), 1: 1.6 / 20 / 9, 2: 3.2 / 24 / 14, 3: 6.5 / 30 / 22, 4: 14 / 38 / 40, 5: unlimited / 46 / up to 1,300.
  At 5 it flies on till you're down: out of the air into space (gravity falling off as the inverse square),
  hovering when Space is let go, F / Ctrl down (braking), W A S D faster the higher you are (up to 2.6 km/s,
  Shift twice that far out) - and the world whose ground is nearest takes over ("Over <world>"), not a gas
  giant: fly to another planet and land on foot. HUD: the charge bar ("JET L<n>") or, at 5, height and speed,
  over the where-you-are box.
- **Town names**: every empire's towns were named from the Minoan list; now each its own (TOWN_NAMES: the
  Attic demes, Laconia's villages, the Argolid's towns, Ionia's cities, the Cyclades' old settlements).
- Guide: the controls line and "The jet pack". Test: test_jump_and_jet_pack (a tap: a jump 1-2 m, the jump
  and fall clips, no leap; held at level 0: higher, the jet clip, the charge burnt and back; level 5: out of
  the air, hovering when let go). Shots retaken.

Numbers: test climbs - level 0 ~6.3 m; level 5: 120 m in 1.5 s, 3.5 km in 12 s, 560 m/s; frame rate within
every baseline.

cosmos_walker.gd, cosmos_hud.gd; scripts/sim/upgrades.gd; scripts/world/life/cosmos_town.gd; tests/test_cosmos.gd;

## 2026-11-22 - Docking without a cut: the ports under the platforms; the stations' law and guns; sieges

Asked: "about stations i dont like that the ship is teleported in a hanger, i want the ships both player's
and npc ships to be lowered in a common hangar area and also the station to have other areas like bars,
lounges, offices, with views outside but also detail terminals etc, i want also npcs that walk around with
dialogue options and the ability to give me missions. Also stations should be armed with very powerful
weapons, committing a crime should give you a fine by the station but committing a very serious crime like
intentionally destroying a ship would lead to being destroyed by the station. Stations in case of war should
be attacked and even be damaged as we did in the 2d version - in that case the stations will require goods
that help it repair itself and will ask for protecting with good rewards"; plus my list: banners moving,
crews carrying crates and at terminals, traders in the hangar.

Done:
- **The port** (CosmosStation): under each landing platform a module hung from it - a floor 60 m below the
  pads' tops (where their lifts stop), the platform's underside its roof (round the pads' shafts), walls, and
  past the platform's outer edge a 40 m strip with a band of windows (glass, lit trim, mullions, lamps) along
  the station's outer wall. The old shafts gone (the lift's way is the hall now). port_transform(i): its frame.
- **CosmosHangar rewritten as the port's inside** (built when you're given a pad - the mesh on a worker, its
  people a frame each - parented to the station, freed once you've flown off): the **hall** (the lifts come
  down into it: rings of light, hazard stripes; pillars or columns by empire, the frieze, banners, the
  emblem great on its wall, stacks of crates, a gantry crane, lamp panels round the shafts), a wall with
  doors and windows onto the ships, the **concourse** (benches, plants, a light line), and a row of rooms
  24 m wide along the windows: **services** (five terminals - market, outfitting, shipyard, designer,
  reputation - each a console with lit keys, a tilted screen, two side screens; benches; the emblem in the
  floor), **bar** (a lit gold-topped counter, stools, shelves of bottles, tables with chairs by the windows),
  **lounge** (sofas facing out, armchair groups, rugs, plants), **harbour office** (desks with screens and
  chairs, cabinets, a great traffic display; the missions terminal), **stores** (shelving racks of crates).
  Room walls panelled (a dado, pilasters with gold heads, a lit cornice), lamp strips and coffers overhead,
  each room its light (warm in the bar, cool in the office), signs over the doors. Repairs: a terminal in
  the hall. You walk it (rects of floor joined by doorways, furniture to walk round; the camera stops at its
  walls - its own boxes).
- **Its people** (19, the empire's own): dock workers about the hall, two carrying crates between the stacks
  and the lifts, two guards at the doors, clerks at the terminals, a bartender, spacers at the bar, harbour
  officers at their desks, travellers in the lounge and walking room to room by the concourse (routes by the
  doors). Far ones' animations paused. **E to talk** (CosmosHangar.person_near): a greeting by their work,
  then Who are you? / Any news? (the sector's latest) / Any work for me? - one of the station's missions, its
  pay, Accept / Not now (Missions.accept) / Farewell.
- **Docking without a cut** (Cosmos): the lift lowers the ship (9 s) down its shaft into the hall, the
  shutters slide shut over it once it's below the deck - no fade, no hall far off; docked there, the lift
  stays down. Undocking: the shutters open, up the lift. Ships round you are kept (not cleared). No sun
  shadows while docked (the roof would shade everything).
- **Traders too** (CosmosNpcShip): set down on a pad, down its lift into the hall (shutters shut), 40-90 s
  unloading, then up and away - parked by your ship when they're on your platform.
- **The law** (CosmosLaw, new): firing on a trader or a patrol near a station - a 250 dr fine (what you
  can't pay is owed: no pad till it's paid, paid when you ask if you can). Destroying one, or firing on a
  station (unless at war with it / striking it - then it takes the damage) - WANTED for 15 minutes: the
  system's stations open fire on you, its patrols hunt you, no pad - till your ship is lost. Stations of an
  empire that holds you hostile shoot at you too.
- **Station guns**: eight heavy turrets a station (two at each platform's outer corners: a drum, a turning
  head, twin long barrels; the empire's look), firing heavy bolts (48 a hit at you - a few seconds under them
  is death; 14 at raiders and invaders) within 4.5 km.
- **Sieges in your system**: an invasion fleet besieging it is there in ships (up to 5 out at once):
  "<empire> warships" circling the station they besiege, firing on its parts (each hit 0.12% of its
  condition; explosions on it), its guns answering. Each destroyed: your defence missions (on_enemy_killed),
  its fleet one smaller (Fleets.ship_lost), 300-500 dr and standing with the defenders if you did it.
- **Hails**: a station besieged or burning hails you as you come within 30 km: "Any ship, any ship! ..." -
  its defence and repair jobs (Missions.crisis_offers) to accept there and then.
- **Damaged stations burn**: explosions on them, more the worse they are.
- **Banners move**: the empire shader sways banners at their foot (stations 1.4 m, inside 0.18 m).
- Fixed: missions generated from the 3D game read the stations' names off the map mirror's stand-ins
  (station_name was missing: errors).

Frame rate: the port's room lights are lit only near the camera (within 34 m), its people far away stand
still (60 m) and aren't drawn (110 m); the hall has no lights of its own (the overhead "sun"). In a
station's hangar: 600 fps at first, 665 after (baseline 883 - the old hall was a bare box).
Numbers: port hall 160 x 350 m (small pads) / 290 x 290 m (big), 33.6 m high; rooms 24 x 24 m, 7.5 m high;
10 / 8 rooms; 7 terminals; 19 people; lift 60 m in 9 s; 8 turrets; fine 250 dr; wanted 15 min.

## 2026-11-22 - The jet pack: dust, roar, heat haze, hard landings; the ship comes for you in space

Asked (from my list): jet pack polish - landing dust and a thrust sound, nozzle heat shimmer, fall damage,
in space a marker to your ship and the ship picking you up.

Done (CosmosWalker, Cosmos, CosmosHud):
- **Dust**: landing at 4 m/s or more kicks up a ring of dust puffs (more and bigger the harder), and the
  jet's blast raises dust off the ground while you're under 3.5 m - soft ragged clouds in the planet's
  ground colour (dust.gdshader, new: lit through from behind), drifting out and fading in 1.6 s.
- **Sound**: a thud on landing (louder the harder); the jet's roar while it fires (louder climbing).
- **Heat haze** under each nozzle (shimmer.gdshader, new: the view behind bent by drifting noise).
- **Hard landings**: over 13 m/s (a fall of ~7.7 m) you're hurt, 7 hp a m/s over - the jet held on the way
  down brakes it. A jump or a jet hop is safe.
- **Your ship's marker** when you're off the ground and away from it: a diamond on it ("Your ship", its
  distance), an arrow at the screen's edge when it's off-screen.
- **The pickup**: flying free higher than 120 m (the top level's pack - out of the air, in space), B: "Your
  ship is coming for you" - it flies from wherever it is (from orbit if it's away) to beside you in 8 s and
  you're aboard, at the controls, flying. The where-you-are box says so ("B: it comes for you").
- CosmosWarm: the dust, the haze, the ports' two-sided glass.
- Test: test_fall_and_space_pickup (3 m: unhurt; 30 m: hurt; flying free 400 m up: called, aboard).

Files: scripts/world/player/cosmos_walker.gd, cosmos_hud.gd; scripts/world/space/cosmos.gd;
scripts/world/models/cosmos_warm.gd; shaders/world/dust.gdshader, shimmer.gdshader (new); tests/test_cosmos.gd.

## 2026-11-22 - The people weathered; aprons and heads that no longer clip

Asked (from my list): weathering on the people; the apron and head clipping.

Done:
- **Weathering** (shaders/pbr_vc.gdshader - every character's merged PBR): grime up from the feet to ~0.9 m
  in splashes, dust on upward faces, chipped paint (dark worn metal, a darker rim; painted parts only, a few
  more low down), scratches through the paint where it's worn, slight unevenness of colour and roughness all
  over; glowing parts kept clean; chips and scratches fading with distance (no shimmer); a `weathering`
  strength. It's placed by the rest pose (CosmosModels.merged stores each vertex's rest position and its
  normal's up in CUSTOM1), so it stays on the parts as they move. CosmosModels hands every character
  material the shared noise as soon as it exists.
- **The apron** (the empires' android, minoan.py): split down the middle, each half skinned to the pelvis at
  the top blending to its own thigh below - it swings with the legs in strides and kicks instead of the
  thighs pushing through it; sits 1 cm further out, flares more at the hem.
- **Heads**: fists in the fighting clips went through the jaws, snouts and brow horns of every skin - the
  heads now sit higher and further back on the neck, the nose a little up (Mn.grow back=). Head/arm overlap
  across every clip: from 1,800-10,000 face pairs a skin to none.
- **The Minoan cape** swings back clear of the knees and shins when running.

Numbers: triangles +3% a skin (e.g. Minoan 40,772 -> 41,824; Athenian 32,908 -> 33,796).

## 2026-11-22 - The port's rooms furnished properly; each service its own panel; sitting down; collisions

Asked: "in the bar the npcs dont have the correct animation of sitting in a chair, also the tables have the
same texture as the floor while the chairs near the tables are just cubes. Also when i use services they open
the tab menu, remove those tabs from tab menu and make them dedicated panel accessed only through station
services, i dont want a replicated functionality. I see also that npcs have no animations for carrying boxes
around. Some collisions are not correct and i can pass through some obstacles at least partially"; then "the
player also need animation for sitting on chairs".

Done:
- **Wood** (the empire shader's new zone, EmpireKit.WOOD): long grain warped a little, fibres, a satin varnish.
- **Furniture** (CosmosHangar): chairs (four turned legs, a cushioned seat at 0.46 m, two back posts, a padded
  back, a top rail), armchairs (a deep body, arms, a raked back, gold feet), bar stools (a weighted foot, a
  column, a foot ring, a cushion at 0.80 m), pedestal tables (a wooden top with a gold rim); the bar's counter
  wood with a foot rail and wooden shelves; the lounge's rows of armchairs facing the windows round low
  wooden tables; the office desks wooden (sides, drawers with gold pulls, a modesty panel, a screen on its
  stand, keys) with a chair at each. Upholstery in the empire's accent colour.
- **Seats**: every chair, armchair and stool is a seat; the bar's spacers, the harbour officers and the
  lounge's travellers sit in them (the sitting clips when their models have them). **You can sit**: E beside a
  free seat - "Sit down"; move or E - "Stand up".
- **Each service its own panel**: a terminal opens only its service (the station menu's single mode: no tab
  bar, no keys to the others; its title the station and the service; Close / Esc steps away, docked still).
  The Sell service, which had no terminal, has one now: **Salvage**, in the stores.
- **Collisions**: every piece of furniture its footprint; pushed out of them twice a step (out of one, not
  into the next); the port's people and the traders' ships parked on its lifts solid too; the plants stop
  the camera.
- Test: the docking test sits down and stands up, checks the market opens alone, the Salvage terminal.
